7d4b5b5f75e6544cd0a3bdd6adaca054a49948c9.summary: Recorded Future's Insikt Group reports two Scanbox campaigns detected in early March 2019: a strategic web compromise of a Pakistani government passport tracking page, and a spoofed Central Tibetan Administration website. It says the attackers likely aimed to profile visitors' devices for follow-on intrusions. It assesses with low confidence that Chinese state-sponsored actors conducted them. Scanbox is a reconnaissance framework written in JavaScript and PHP that can log keystrokes.

7dd057ab41b4f45ffa29e29508f2e9fe438236cb.summary: Analyst write-up reverse engineering an AMOS Stealer macOS sample disguised as an installer disk image. The sample was undetected by security vendors on March 11, 2025. Using LLDB and Binary Ninja, the author bypassed anti-VM checks and extracted a hidden AppleScript payload. The report describes theft of browser data, desktop crypto wallet files and Telegram session data, archiving to a ZIP file, and upload to a hardcoded C2 server. It includes a YARA rule and references 196 file hashes.

7d655727d9e5f37fe4c483e2a78351ef28e8e03d.summary: Microsoft's May 2021 analysis of Phorpiex, a long-running botnet used for sextortion and spam, bot-loader distribution, cryptocurrency mining and ransomware delivery (including Avaddon, Knot and others). It describes spread through USB drives and email, a shift of command-and-control to IP and DGA domains, registry changes that disable security tools, and bot loader encounters in 160 countries from December 2020 to February 2021. The report also gives Microsoft Defender detection guidance.

7d4f77e0ed23b61a33a96469a8c5d411ca1aac01.summary: Kaspersky Lab's February 2015 report on Carbanak, a backdoor used in a campaign against banks and financial institutions since late 2013. Infections used spear phishing emails and exploit kits, and the attackers spied on staff through video capture before moving to SWIFT, ATM and banking systems. The report cites cumulative losses of up to 1 billion USD, with 100 banking entities affected at the time of writing.

hedges: The report says the motivation appears to be financial gain as opposed to espionage.
The report believes attackers also redirected traffic to exploit kits; this is stated as a belief, not confirmed.
Indicators point to a possible Chinese origin for the exploits, and the report says this could just be a red herring.
Losses of up to 1 billion USD come from victims and law enforcement; the report says Carbanak may be responsible for losses as high as 1 billion USD.
Victim countries come from geolocation of infected IPs; the report says this does not necessarily mean all these victims are banking entities.
As far as the report knows, none of the abused services were attacked and no specific vulnerability within them was exploited.
The report believes the privilege escalation attempt against a Kaspersky product is not relevant and that attackers adapt tools to victim defenses.
The report says it is possible the attacks were coordinated to maximise returns before industry-wide information sharing.

It describes CARBANAK's desktop video recording feature, the custom video file format and player that worked with it, and a recovered recording of an operator preparing post-exploitation tools. The report links the toolset to FIN7 and speculates about a front company, and it marks those points as speculation.
